core_obligations: Name the represented objects (proof lines 8770-8773): let M be the object of D(O) represented by both I^bullet and (I')^bullet, and L the object represented by both L^bullet and (L')^bullet.

Compute both H^0 groups (proof lines 8774-8781): by the same-chapter result on internal homs into a K-injective complex, each of H^0(SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet, (I')^bullet)) and H^0(SheafHom^bullet((L')^bullet, I^bullet)) is the sheaf associated to U -> Hom_{D(O_U)}(L|_U, M|_U).

Conclude (proof lines 8781-8785): the displayed map of complexes induces an isomorphism on H^0 of the two complexes that are quasi-isomorphic to the objects displayed, hence it is a quasi-isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Read off the objects M and L represented by the two pairs of complexes.
Identify both H^0 groups with the same sheafified presheaf of derived homs.
Conclude that the displayed map is a quasi-isomorphism.
This is what makes RSheafHom well defined on D(O) in both variables.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the internal hom complex is independent of the chosen K-injective representatives in the first variable and of the chosen representative in the second, up to quasi-isomorphism (statement lines 8753-8767). The proof is short but hinges on the representative bookkeeping: one names the objects M and L represented by the two quasi-isomorphic pairs and then invokes the same-chapter description of H^0 of an internal hom into a K-injective complex as the sheafified presheaf U -> Hom_{D(O_U)}(L|_U, M|_U), which is symmetric in the two choices (proof lines 8770-8781). The claim is H2: one identification of two H^0 groups, with no further construction.
